summary: This is a Makefile that defines a build target. When you run 'make build', it compiles a C source file called main.c using the gcc compiler and produces an executable program named app.

explanations.1: The 'build:' line defines a target — a named recipe that you can run with the 'make' command, so 'make build' will execute the commands below it.
explanations.2: The leading tab character (shown as \t) is required by Make syntax; it tells Make that this is a command to execute. The command itself runs gcc (the C compiler) on main.c and uses the '-o' flag to name the output executable 'app'.
